metadata.title: Genesis: A Machine-Native Cognitive Architecture
metadata.description:
Genesis is a two-layer cognitive architecture that runs on a single machine with no external model — no transformer, no pretrained weights. A Rust daemon integrates an 18-chemical neuromodulatory substrate, an electrochemical ion layer, a sourced sleep–wake network (Booth/Diniz Behn), active inference over its own chemical trajectory, and memory consolidation on a 5 Hz body clock; a Python cognitive layer handles perception, reasoning, compositional language, and self-modeling over a self-built semantic network. The system is embodied on real silicon: hardware sensors drive neurochemistry, neurochemistry drives real CPU control, and a physical field probe closes a measured phase-lock between modeled brain waves and actual processor dynamics. The project exists to show that large language models are not the only way to build a mind — and that the functional machinery the leading theories of consciousness describe (global workspace broadcast, embodied self-modeling, affective interoception, higher-order representation) can be implemented and inspected in the open. Source: https://github.com/MindyRenee/Genesis

Version 0.2.0 supersedes the 0.1.0 snapshot: schema v5 (3,480-byte core state), 5 Hz tick, sleep staged by the Booth/Diniz Behn network rather than adenosine thresholds, the electrochemical ion layer, per-person dyadic signatures, the physical-field coupling channel and its assays, and revised ARC practice evidence.
